[[File:EclipseHangsOminouslyInSpace-FoC.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class Star Dreadnought]] gained notoriety for its [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]].]]
'''Star Dreadnought''', sometimes spelled '''Star Dreadnaught''', was a formal designation for some of the largest and strongest [[Warship/Legends|Warships]] in the starfleets of regional<ref name="Attack of the Clones: Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> and [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] navies.<ref name="ROTS:ICS">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> Under the [[Anaxes War College System/Legends|Anaxes War College System]], "Star Dreadnought" referred to any warship in excess of five kilometers in length.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

The term "[[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]]" was also applied colloquially (and sometimes derisively) to some of these ships by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. In these cases, Star Dreadnoughts were noted as being the largest Super Star Destroyers.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref><ref name="Starship Battles Preview 1">{{SWMiniCite|set=Starship Battles|parent=1}}</ref> In turn, the lower-case term '''star dreadnought''' could be used to describe Super Star Destroyers in general.<ref name="SOTG07">[[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'', Saga Edition]]</ref>

Various classes of Star Dreadnoughts were known to have served in the [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] [[Kuati Sector Forces|defense fleets]],<ref name="Attack of the Clones: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]],<ref name="Clone Wars Volume 6: On the Fields of Battle">''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Volume 6: On the Fields of Battle]]''</ref><ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]],<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]]<ref name="Crimson Empire">''[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire]]''</ref> and the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Fleet]].<ref name="The Unifying Force">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref> Their sizes eclipsed most conventional warships, peaking with the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class]] at 19 km in length,<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> and the [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class]], with its unequaled mass and weaponry.<ref name="SOTG07" />

==History==
===Private service===
During the centuries leading up to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], important and rich galactic sectors were protected by private self-defense forces.<ref name="Attack of the Clones: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> The [[Kuat sector/Legends|Kuat sector]] had among its arsenal the eight-kilometer [[Mandator-class Star Dreadnaught|''Mandator''-class Star Dreadnought]], a class that entered service at some point prior to [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]].<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> They were large battleships equipped with heavy firepower, but had a limited range on their hyperdrives. ''Mandator''s were primarily used to protect the valuable [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], as well as defend the general sector.<ref name="Attack of the Clones: Incredible Cross-Sections" />

===Clone Wars era and beyond===
By the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], seven of what KDY classified as Star Dreadnoughts were in service: three defended Kuat, while the [[Azure sector/Legends|Azure]], [[Ixtlar sector/Legends|Ixtlar]], [[Alsaka sector/Legends|Alsaka]] and [[Humbarine sector/Legends|Humbarine sectors]] had one each.<ref name="EGW" />

As the Clone Wars raged, heavier warships as well as increased loyalty were demanded, and [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] pushed through legislation that made all home fleets fall under the centralized command of the restored Republic Navy.<ref name="SWR71">[[Republic 71|''Republic'' 71]]</ref> The Kuat Drive Yards produced the faster, more heavily-armed and -armored [[Mandator II-class Star Dreadnaught/Legends|''Mandator II'']] during this period.<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /><ref name="DBRAC">{{DB|starship|republicattackcruiser|Republic attack cruiser}}</ref> Three new ''Mandator II''s were built, while three earlier ''Mandator''s were uparmored and refitted. All of them saw use in defending the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] against Separatist incursions.<ref name="EGW" />

Following the war's end, the new Imperial Navy began the [[Sarlacc Project]], to build a new huge warship design to serve as a flagship for the entire Navy. This [[Super Star Destroyer prototype]], twelve kilometers in length, was [[Battle of Byss|destroyed]] by early Rebel elements over [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] before its completion. Despite its destruction, it managed to inspire future Star Dreadnaught designs,<ref name="DOD">''[[Dawn of Defiance]]''</ref> and the Empire ordered the construction of four new dreadnoughts, each nineteen kilometers in length.<ref name="EGW" />

===Galactic Civil War era===
[[File:WrathBDZ-EGTW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An [[Assertor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Assertor''-class Star Dreadnought]] leading a [[Base Delta Zero/Legends|Base Delta Zero]] operation]]
The Star Dreadnought concept was not without opposition in the Imperial Navy. Many traditionalists saw the enormous ships as far too expensive and inefficient in comparison to [[Patrol ship/Legends|patrol boats]], [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] and [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] for policing space. Likewise, the Navy's growing number of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] carried unmatched firepower should the Imperial Navy fight a fleet battle. To traditionalists, [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruisers]] and dreadnoughts, lumped together under the derisive tag "[[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyers]]" (which later spread to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] through Imperial defectors), seemed to be egotistical constructions rather than pieces of a coherent military strategy.<ref name="EGW" />

As the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] heated up, various new Star Dreadnought designs were shelved mid-production due to countless credits and talented engineers being diverted to the creation of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], with its destruction being the only reason they were able to continue.<ref name="EGW" /> Skeptical of [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] like the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] worked hard to come up with reasonable alternatives that could hold their own in the face of massive centralization of power, and reluctantly embraced the Star Dreadnought.<ref name="SOTG01">''[[Starships of the Galaxy]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> With the Death Star's destruction, they became the Empire's mightiest weapons, designed to be so powerful that the mere threat of their deployment would pacify multiple [[Sector/Legends|sectors]].<ref name="EGW" />

Among the achievements of this era was the ''Executor''-class design. By this point, the Star Dreadnought designation was known to Imperial [[Military Oversight Committee/Legends|oversight committees]] as representing extraordinarily large and heavily armed warships. In order to avoid controversy in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], [[Imperial Navy/Legends|naval]] documents simply classified the new Star Dreadnought as a new class of Star Destroyer, understating its size, role and armament.<ref name="Starship Battles Preview 1" /> The Star Dreadnoughts were also viewed by the Galactic Empire as useful for psychological warfare purposes, to cow various systems. This made the ships' development worth the expenses.

When fielded, these ships gained notoriety as [[Command ship/Legends|command ships]] for large-scale forces as well as being heavy weapons platforms, with the [[Executor/Legends|lead vessel]] serving as [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] personal [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]].<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> These ships were some of the largest in the galaxy, second only to battlestations like the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. Though their sluggish speed, massive size, and poor maneuverability proved to be severe weaknesses, they were unmatched in firepower by any other frontline ship and incredibly resilient to direct assaults.
Another design, the [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class]], which began construction around the time of the ''Executor''{{'s}} early deployment, became dreadful weapons of terror, as each ship was equipped with a [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] for penetrating planetary shields and pulverizing enemy ships.<ref name="DESB">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="Underworld: A Galaxy of Scum and Villainy">{{InsiderCite|89|Underworld: A Galaxy of Scum and Villainy}}</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>

As the Empire [[Imperial Civil War|split into warring factions]] following the Emperor's death, its formidable fleet of Dreadnoughts was divided up between various Warlords. Despite the imposing threat of these classes, most were either destroyed by sabotage or in battle, or captured by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], leaving few rogue Star Dreadnoughts still active at the end of the Civil War.<ref name="SOTG07" />

===New Republic counterparts===
[[File:Viscount-profile.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Viscount-class Star Defender|''Viscount''-class Star Defender]] was conceived to challenge [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] Star Dreadnoughts and other heavy warships.]]
The New Republic initially regarded Star Dreadnoughts as inflexible and inefficient, preferring a combination of smaller-platform capital ships and starfighters for its fleets. Consequently, the [[New Class Modernization Program]] did not include new [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruiser]] or dreadnought designs. However, the experience of [[Operation Shadow Hand]], where some twelve Star Dreadnoughts led a renewed Imperial assault out of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], the [[Orinda campaign]], where they proved to have no counter against the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant's]] [[Reaper (Executor-class)|''Reaper'']], ''[[Megador]]'' and [[Dominion (Star Dreadnought)|''Dominion'']] dreadnoughts, and finally the [[Black Fleet Crisis]], the New Republic realized the need for bigger and stronger capital ships to deter would-be attackers. Running low on captured vessels of this size, new dreadnought classes were designed that were meant to be Republic counterparts to the Star Dreadnoughts.<ref name="Starship Battles Preview 1" /><ref name="EGW" />

The [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Viscount-class Star Defender|''Viscount''-class]] [[Star Defender]]s were new directions for Republic ship-building, away from the compact designs of the [[New Class Modernization Program|New Class]] program.<ref name="Vector Prime">''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]''</ref> They were among the largest classes produced by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and saw heavy duty in the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], becoming part of the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Fleet]], when the New Republic was reorganized into the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]].<ref name="Force Heretic I: Remnant">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic I: Remnant]]''</ref>

At some point following the Second Galactic Civil War, heavy warships like the [[Star Defender]]s and Star Dreadnoughts were phased out of service, citing the expenses in operating the various designs.<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>
By [[130 ABY]], neither the re-emergent [[Fel Empire|Galactic Empire]] nor the remainder of the Galactic Alliance used the term for their present ships,<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref> though the [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer]] was known to have combined some aspects of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] and the ''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought.<ref name="SOTG07" />

==Known Star Dreadnought designs==
===[[Assertor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Assertor''-class Star Dreadnought]]===
The '''''Assertor''-class''' was a Star Dreadnought used by the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. A known example of this class was the ''Wrath'', which participated in a [[Base Delta Zero/Legends|Base Delta Zero]] operation.<ref name="EGW" /> Its primary role was acting as a sector command and control ship.<ref name="Lead by Example">''[[Lead by Example]]''</ref>

===[[Bellator-class dreadnought/Legends|''Bellator''-class dreadnought]]===
The ''Bellator''-class dreadnought was a successor design to the ''Mandator''-class and ''Mandator II''-class Star Dreadnoughts, being built primarily with speed in mind in contrast with its "cousin," the ''Mandator III''-class dreadnought. Several ships of this class were seen at [[Naval Station Validusia/Legends|Naval Station ''Validusia'']], a fleet gathering between Ozzel's promotion and the Battle of Hoth, and in the [[Byss Defense Fleet|forces]] of the resurrected Emperor Palpatine in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]]. A ''Bellator''-class was escorted by a ''Procursator''-class Star Destroyer in orbit of Byss.<ref name="DEI">[[Dark Empire 2|''Dark Empire'' 2]]</ref>

===[[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class dreadnought]]===
The 17.5km '''''Eclipse''-class''' was fitted with a [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] as its primary armament and its reactor took up much of the interior space.<ref name="DESB" /> Two vessels were constructed in secret over a ten year period, and fielded during [[Operation Shadow Hand]]. Both were destroyed.<ref name="SOTG07" /> According to the ''Imperial Handbook'', the official field manual for the Imperial Military, the ''Eclipse''-class as well as its sister design the ''Sovereign''-class were intended to revolutionize naval combat and ensure Imperial dominance through the next century.<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

===[[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]]===
[[File:Super_Star_Destroyer_AorCR.png|thumb|right|250px|An ''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought dwarfs surrounding ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers.]]
The '''''Executor''-class''' was a successful line of Star Dreadnoughts that came in several variants, and was believed to be the "ultimate" in Star Dreadnought design in its time.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> The 19km battleship model was considered a valuable prize to many commanders, and receiving command of a ship was a high honor, sometimes bestowed upon an officer as a gift by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] himself.<ref name="TNEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Over a dozen ships were built and fielded.

===[[Mandator-class Star Dreadnaught|''Mandator''-class Star Dreadnaught]]===
The '''''Mandator''-class''' served in the private sector fleets of the [[Kuat sector/Legends|Kuat sector]], being designed and fielded in the final decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Attack of the Clones: Incredible Cross-Sections" />

===[[Mandator II-class Star Dreadnaught/Legends|''Mandator II''-class Star Dreadnaught]]===
The '''''Mandator II''-class''' was a new model of the ''Mandator'' design and served as part of the Republic Navy during the Clone Wars. Its power-generation facilities matched that of almost 1,000 [[Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|light Separatist destroyers]].<ref name="ROTS:ICS" />

===[[Mandator III-class dreadnought|''Mandator III''-class dreadnought]]===
The '''''Mandator III''-class''' was a newer model of the ''Mandator'' design and served in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Unlike the previous ''Mandator''{{'s}} or its "cousin," the [[Bellator-class dreadnought/Legends|''Bellator''-class dreadnought]], the ''Mandator III''-class was specifically designed to act as a heavy weapons platform, and had a length of 12,000 meters.

===[[Sovereign-class Super Star Destroyer|''Sovereign''-class Super Star Destroyer]]===
The '''''Sovereign''-class''' was based on the ''Eclipse''-class and meant to be a smaller, cheaper design for mass-production.<ref name="DESB" /> Construction on the first four ships began around 0 ABY, but they were all ultimately destroyed around the time of Palpatine's final death and the [[Destruction of Byss]].<ref name="TJASB">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> According to the ''Imperial Handbook'', the official field manual for the Imperial Military, the ''Sovereign''-class as well as its sister design the ''Eclipse''-class were intended to revolutionize naval combat and ensure Imperial dominance through the next century.<ref name="IHB" />

===[[Sarlacc Project]]===
The '''Sarlacc Project''' was aimed at developing a flagship for the then-newly created [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. The end result was a warship 12km long, covered in various armaments. The vessel [[Battle of Byss|was destroyed]] in a partially-completed state, a few years after its construction began. Despite the loss, it was used as inspiration for the later ''Executor''-class.<ref name="DOD" />

===[[Vengeance-class dreadnought|''Vengeance''-class Star Dreadnought]]===
The ''Vengeance''-class was a 19km long Star Dreadnought line with at least three vessels produced. They had a sleeker design than the Executor class Dreadnought. The [[Vengeance (Vengeance-class)|''Vengeance'']] was the flagship of Dark Jedi and Imperial Inquisitor [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] from before the Battle of Endor to his death in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]]. The [[Javelin (Vengeance-class)|''Javelin'']] anchored one of the fleets to reconquer the Core Worlds during [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], but was destroyed during the [[Imperial Civil War]] when it rammed a Torpedo Sphere that guarded the planet [[Chasin]].<ref name="EGW" />

==Star Dreadnought analogs==
===[[Death Star II/Legends|''Death Star II'']]===
Although not a dreadnaught in the general sense, the '''''Death Star II''''', due to its heavy firepower and powerful role, was frequently referred to by both Rebels and Imperials as being comparable to such during the Battle of Endor.<ref name="ROTJc">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (1983)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' (1983)]]</ref>

===''[[Eye of Palpatine]]''===
The '''''Eye of Palpatine''''' was a dreadnaught larger in overall size than the largest Super Star Destroyers, fielded in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="COTJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> although in terms of length was comparable in size to the ''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought and ''Vengeance''-class dreadnought at 19 kilometers.<ref name="DSOWM">''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref> It was meant to pick up Imperial forces along a secret route that lead to a planet where [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were in hiding, but malfunctioned due to Jedi sabotage and disappeared. [[12 ABY/Legends|Decades later]], the ship was reactivated in a ploy to get more power for the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], but was ultimately destroyed by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="COTJ" />

===[[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']]===
The '''''Tarkin''''' superweapon was developed as a superlaser bed, a intermediary between the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station and the Death Star II. It was created from the hull design of an ''Eclipse''-class dreadnought prototype.

===[[Viscount-class Star Defender|''Viscount''-class Star Defender]]===
One of several Star Defender classes, the '''''Viscount''-class''' was built by Mon Calamari and fielded by the New Republic and [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].<ref name="Starship Battles Preview 1" />

===[[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Kor Chokk]] grand cruiser===
The '''Grand Cruiser''' was a Yuuzhan Vong analog of heavy Super Star Destroyers and used in fleet battles during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="TNJOSB">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In Naval terminology, dreadnought is generally synonymous with [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]] constructed after and influenced by [[Wikipedia:HMS Dreadnought (1906)|HMS ''Dreadnought'']]. This term was sometimes used for great ships in ''Star Wars'', like the ''Executor'',<ref name="DVS">"[[Darth Vader Strikes]]"</ref> the ''Eye of Palpatine''<ref name="COTJ" /> and the [[Death Star II/Legends|''Death Star II'']].<ref name="ROTJc" />

The designation "Star Dreadnought" was first explicitly used in ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' for the ''Mandator''-class, and the ''Executor''-class was given the designation in ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''. ''Inside the Worlds'' also stated that "Super Star Destroyer" was used in "Rebel slang", while [[Starship Battles (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Starship Battles Preview 1'']] explained that the term was invented and popularized by Imperial personnel.

The term "Star Dreadnought" (or "Star Dreadnaught") is disliked by some fans who prefer the term "Super Star Destroyer", which already referred to many different ships.
Since the Expanded Universe renaissance introduced by [[West End Games]] had sources specifically divide warships into different types depending on their size and power, some fans welcomed what they saw as a necessary additions to explain all the differently sized Super Star Destroyers seen throughout decades of publishing. Others considered the various redesignations and redefinitions contradictory and unnecessary, accepting the use of Super Star Destroyer as a general category. Despite different naval nomenclature being used by various authors, [[Curtis Saxton]] was widely seen as responsible for the change in designations.

Much of the criticism towards the term "Star Dreadnought" stem from the belief that it's applying terminology to ship names that were not originally created to fit with the English naval hierarchy and that only recent authors like Saxton have used it in such a fashion. I.e. a [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] and a [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Star Cruiser]] are not analogous to a naval Destroyer and a naval Cruiser and are equivalent in size and role, ships of size comparable to Star Dreadnoughts like the [[Subjugator-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Subjugator''-class heavy cruiser]] lack the description, and the existing [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class]] ship is smaller than all three. As well, the term Star Dreadnought was initially seen as largely redundant with the pre-existing term Super Star Destroyer, as at the time the term Star Dreadnought was first used, Super Star Destroyers categorized as Star Cruisers and Star Battlecruisers have neither been introduced nor were they specifically identified, leaving Star Dreadnoughts the only category within Super Star Destroyer with any ships in it.
